title: Ezekiel Chapter 34 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 34 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 34 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 34.

questions.question: What did the Lord say to the shepherds of Israel in Ezekiel 34:2?
options: Woe be to the shepherds that do feed themselves!
questions.correctAnswer: Woe be to the shepherds that do feed themselves!
questions.explanation: The Lord's message to the shepherds was a warning, emphasizing their failure to care for the flock as stated in Ezekiel 34:2.

questions.question: True or False: The shepherds of Israel fed the flock according to Ezekiel 34:3.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:3 states that the shepherds killed those that were fed but did not feed the flock, indicating their neglect.

questions.question: What has not been done to the diseased according to Ezekiel 34:4?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:4 clearly states that the diseased have not been strengthened, highlighting the negligence of the shepherds.

questions.question: True or False: The flock was scattered because there was a shepherd according to Ezekiel 34:5.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:5 indicates that the flock was scattered because there was no shepherd, leading to their vulnerability.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 34:6, where did the sheep wander?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:6 describes how the sheep wandered through all the mountains and high hills, indicating their dispersion.

questions.question: What does the Lord declare He will do in Ezekiel 34:11?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:11 states that the Lord will search His sheep and seek them out, demonstrating His care and responsibility.

questions.question: True or False: The shepherds sought after the lost sheep according to Ezekiel 34:8.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:8 states that the shepherds did not search for the flock, highlighting their neglect.

questions.question: What will happen to the shepherds according to Ezekiel 34:10?
options: They will cease from feeding the flock.
questions.correctAnswer: They will cease from feeding the flock.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:10 specifies that the Lord will require His flock at the hand of the shepherds and cause them to cease from feeding.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 34, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:2 instructs the prophet to prophesy against the shepherds as the first action.

questions.question: What did the Lord say would happen to the flock in Ezekiel 34:22?
options: They shall no more be a prey.
questions.correctAnswer: They shall no more be a prey.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:22 states that the Lord will save His flock and they shall no longer be a prey, indicating His protection.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord will deliver His flock from their mouth according to Ezekiel 34:10.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:10 confirms that the Lord will deliver His flock from the mouth of the shepherds, ensuring their safety.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 34:15, what does the Lord say He will do?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:15 states that the Lord will feed His flock, indicating His provision and care.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 34 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 34 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will the Lord do to the shepherds who feed themselves instead of the flock?
questions.explanation: The Lord declares that He is against the shepherds and will require them to cease from feeding themselves, indicating judgment upon those who neglect their responsibilities (Ezekiel 34:10).

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 34, what does the Lord promise to do for His sheep?
questions.explanation: The Lord promises to search for His sheep and seek them out, demonstrating His commitment to care for them despite their scattering (Ezekiel 34:11).

questions.question: What will happen to the flock that has been mistreated by selfish shepherds?
questions.explanation: The Lord states He will save His flock and ensure they are no longer a prey, indicating His protective action over them (Ezekiel 34:22).

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 34:15, what will the Lord do for His flock?
options: I will make them work harder
questions.explanation: The Lord directly states that He will feed His flock, indicating His provision and care (Ezekiel 34:15).

questions.question: True or False: The shepherds of Israel are accused of healing the sick and binding up the broken.
questions.explanation: The text states that the shepherds have not strengthened the diseased or healed the sick, but rather ruled with force and cruelty (Ezekiel 34:4).

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 34:19 say about the flock's food and drink?
options: It is provided by the shepherds
It is scarce and hard to find
questions.explanation: The verse explains that the flock eats what the shepherds have trodden with their feet and drinks what they have fouled, highlighting the neglect of the shepherds (Ezekiel 34:19).

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 34:13, what will the Lord do once He gathers His sheep?
options: He will bring them to their own land
questions.correctAnswer: He will bring them to their own land
questions.explanation: The Lord promises to gather His sheep and bring them to their own land, signifying restoration and care (Ezekiel 34:13).

questions.question: True or False: The Lord will raise up a new shepherd for His flock, according to Ezekiel 34:23.
questions.explanation: The Lord declares that He will set up one shepherd over them, specifically His servant David, who will care for the flock (Ezekiel 34:23).

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 34:16 emphasize about the Lord's actions towards His flock?
options: He will only care for the strong
questions.explanation: The Lord emphasizes that He will seek the lost, bind up the broken, and strengthen the sick, showing His compassion and care for all members of His flock (Ezekiel 34:16).

questions.question: What consequence is described in Ezekiel 34:21 for those who have scattered the flock?
questions.explanation: The verse states that those who have thrust with side and shoulder will face judgment, indicating accountability for their actions against the flock (Ezekiel 34:21).

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 34:25, what will the Lord make with His people?
questions.explanation: The Lord promises to make a covenant of peace with His people, which signifies security and well-being (Ezekiel 34:25).

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 34:18 illustrate the neglect of the shepherds?
options: By showing they cared for the flock
By indicating they ate the good pasture
questions.correctAnswer: By indicating they ate the good pasture
questions.explanation: The verse points out that the shepherds have consumed the good pasture while neglecting the flock, illustrating their selfishness (Ezekiel 34:18).

questions.question: True or False: The Lord will make the evil beasts cease from the land as part of His covenant with His people.
questions.explanation: The Lord promises to cause the evil beasts to cease from the land, ensuring safety for His people as part of His covenant of peace (Ezekiel 34:25).

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 34 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 34.

questions.question: Who does the Lord say will be set up as a shepherd over the flock?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically mentions that the Lord will set up 'my servant David' as a shepherd over them (Ezekiel 34:23).

questions.question: What will the Lord cause to cease out of the land?
questions.explanation: The Lord states He will cause 'the evil beasts to cease out of the land' (Ezekiel 34:25).

questions.question: What does the Lord promise to make with His flock?
questions.explanation: The Lord promises to make 'a covenant of peace' with His flock (Ezekiel 34:25).

questions.question: What will happen to the flock when the Lord breaks the bands of their yoke?
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that they shall be safe in their land after the Lord has broken the bands of their yoke (Ezekiel 34:27).

questions.question: What is the 'plant of renown' that the Lord will raise up for the flock?
questions.explanation: The 'plant of renown' is often interpreted as a reference to the coming Messiah, which is echoed in other prophetic passages (Ezekiel 34:29).

questions.question: In Ezekiel 34:30, who is referred to as the flock of God's pasture?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'the house of Israel' are referred to as 'my flock, the flock of my pasture' (Ezekiel 34:30).

questions.question: True or False: The Lord will judge between cattle and cattle.
questions.explanation: The Lord explicitly states that He will judge between cattle and cattle (Ezekiel 34:20).

questions.question: What will the Lord cause to come down in due season?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that there shall be 'showers of blessing' (Ezekiel 34:26).

questions.question: What literary device is used in the structure of Ezekiel 34:15-16?
questions.explanation: The verses use parallelism by repeating the structure of God's promises to feed and care for His flock (Ezekiel 34:15-16).

questions.question: True or False: The shepherds of Israel were accused of feeding the flock.
questions.explanation: The shepherds were condemned for feeding themselves rather than the flock (Ezekiel 34:2-3).

questions.question: Which other biblical passage is echoed in Ezekiel 34:23 regarding a shepherd?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:23, which mentions the shepherd, is fulfilled in John 10:11 where Christ refers to Himself as the Good Shepherd.

questions.question: What does the Lord promise regarding the safety of His flock?
questions.explanation: The Lord promises that His flock will dwell safely and will not be afraid (Ezekiel 34:28).

questions.question: What is the significance of the term 'flock' in the context of Ezekiel 34?
questions.explanation: The term 'flock' symbolizes the people of Israel, as indicated throughout the chapter, especially in verses discussing their care and protection (Ezekiel 34:31).

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 34 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 34 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the main charge against the shepherds of Israel in Ezekiel 34?
questions.explanation: The charge against the shepherds is clearly stated in Ezekiel 34:2-3, where it says they do not feed the flock but rather feed themselves.

questions.question: What will God do because the shepherds have failed to care for the flock?
options: He will require His flock at their hand
questions.correctAnswer: He will require His flock at their hand
questions.explanation: God declares in Ezekiel 34:10 that He will require the flock from the hands of the shepherds due to their negligence.

questions.question: What does God promise to do for His sheep in Ezekiel 34:11?
options: He will search and seek them out
questions.correctAnswer: He will search and seek them out
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:11 states that God Himself will search for His sheep and seek them out, showing His commitment to care for His people.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 34:16, what does God say He will do for the sick and broken?
options: He will bind up that which is broken
questions.correctAnswer: He will bind up that which is broken
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:16 reveals God's intention to care for those who are broken and sick, indicating His compassion.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 34:23 indicate about the future shepherd?
options: He will be a military leader
He will be a prince among them
questions.correctAnswer: He will be a prince among them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:23 prophesies that God will set up one shepherd over them, specifically stating that His servant David will be their prince.

questions.question: What covenant does God make with His people in Ezekiel 34:25?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 34:25, God makes a covenant of peace, promising safety and security to His people.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 34:29 promise regarding hunger?
options: They will be consumed with hunger
They shall be no more consumed with hunger
They will eat from the beasts
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be no more consumed with hunger
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:29 assures that God's people will not experience hunger anymore, signifying His provision.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 34:6 describe the state of God's sheep?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:6 describes how God's sheep have wandered and are scattered all over the earth, highlighting their vulnerability.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Ezekiel 34:12 when He seeks out His sheep?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 34:12, God's action of seeking out His scattered sheep demonstrates His compassionate nature.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'I will judge between cattle and cattle' in Ezekiel 34:17 imply?
options: God will make distinctions among His people
questions.correctAnswer: God will make distinctions among His people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:17 shows that God will bring judgment and discernment among His people, emphasizing His justice.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 34:30, what will the house of Israel know?
options: That they are not God's people
That the LORD their God is with them
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD their God is with them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:30 states that they will know the presence of the LORD their God, affirming their relationship with Him.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 34:18 criticize about the shepherds' actions?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:18 criticizes the shepherds for treading down the good pasture, showing their selfishness and neglect.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 34:21 indicate about the behavior of the shepherds?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:21 shows that the shepherds have thrust and pushed the diseased, leading to the scattering of the flock.

questions.question: What is the sceptics' claim regarding God's care for His people, and how does Ezekiel 34:11-12 counter this?
options: God does not care for individuals
God actively seeks and cares for His people
questions.correctAnswer: God actively seeks and cares for His people
questions.explanation: Sceptics may claim that God neglects His people, but Ezekiel 34:11-12 demonstrates that He actively seeks out and cares for them.

questions.question: What is indicated by God's promise to deliver His flock in Ezekiel 34:10?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:10 indicates that God will deliver His flock from the mouth of the shepherds, ensuring their protection.
